research_policy.rule: Italian Editorial DNA research must not stop at historical canon. It must trace transformations into current Italian editorial practice and test continuity, mutation, rejection, digital/print hybridity, automation and AI-era judgement.
research_policy.anti_style_rule: Do not infer a timeless Italian look. Track transferable editorial intelligence across eras and distinguish inheritance from revival, quotation, constraint and fashion.

current_2025_2026_evidence.finding: The Bjarke Ingels guest-editor year used a graphic project by Francesco Franchi and Lorenzo Frosi that explicitly revisited Domus of the late 1960s/early 1970s while making each issue's material theme generate cover and opening structure.

Under guest editor Ma Yansong, issue themes continue to alter editorial metaphors and cover logic: fantasy, nature-as-process, collaboration-as-network, movement, repair and memory. Covers function as arguments rather than generic wrappers.

AIAP split Progetto Grafico into a peer-reviewed digital Journal and a practice-oriented print Magazine, giving distinct media forms to distinct editorial functions rather than forcing one format to serve both.
The 2026 issue on automation explicitly asks what remains of design and designer judgement when images, layouts and identities can be generated by prompts, algorithms, templates and platforms.
The cover call requires a modular/pattern composition with no single focal point, able to survive variable overlays of masthead, issue title and service information without losing meaning.

next: Build a continuous family/era bridge from Ponti/Domus and postwar Italian editorial systems through radical/postmodern, Lupi, Franchi and current 2026 practice; then run cross-era blind-transfer and negative-selection tests before capability admission.
